key_insight: Poorer baseline prognosis was associated with greater survival benefit from chemotherapy-containing regimens versus pembrolizumab alone in head and neck and urothelial cancers, with a less certain pattern in lung cancer.
clinical_relevance: These findings question the assumption that immunotherapy alone offers the best benefit–risk balance for patients with poor prognosis, but do not establish individual treatment recommendations.
method: Emulated five first-line treatment trials using US electronic health records from 8,688 patients treated during 2011–2023.
Used machine learning to predict baseline 6-month survival.
Applied overlap-weighted regression to assess differences in 2-year restricted mean survival time across prognosis levels.
evidence_signal: The treatment-benefit difference between poor- and favorable-prognosis groups was 102.4 days in head and neck cancer and 51.4 days in urothelial cancer; colorectal cancer and melanoma showed overall immunotherapy benefit without clear variation by prognosis.
watch_item: Observational target trial emulations remain vulnerable to unmeasured confounding; this study evaluates treatment outcomes rather than AI-driven drug discovery.
paper_title: Baseline Prognosis and Treatment Benefit From First-Line Immunotherapy Strategies: Target Trial Emulations Across Advanced Solid Tumors
